newsitem.title: USA: Campbell says retiree deal approved.
newsitem.headline: Campbell says retiree deal approved.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co said a U.S. District Court had approved its $114.5 million settlement with a group of retired employees who sued the company after it cut its medical benefits in 1992.
"It's been approved by the court," Campbell spokesman Kevin Lowery said.
Under the settlement, Campbell is to pay the $114.5 million to help cover medical costs for the group of 12,000 retirees and their dependents.
Campbell has said the settlement would not affect current earnings because its cost had been reserved against earnings previously.

Under the settlement, a fund established by Campbell will provide managed care coverage, including up to 80 percent of drug costs, through health maintenance organizations, and include an option for continued Medicare participation.
The deal does not affect Campbell employees who retired after the cut in benefits was announced.
